turns.doctor_question: Hello, please have a seat. What brings you in to see me today?
turns.patient_response:
Hi, thank you so much for fitting me in. Um... well, I guess I'm just a little embarrassed to be taking up your time. It's probably just me needing to try harder, but... what finally scared me into coming in is that I just keep making these really dumb technical mistakes at work. 

I work in video editing and camera operation, and lately I've been doing things I absolutely know better than to make. Like, um, labeling camera cards wrong, or missing a timecode note... or exporting a client cut with the wrong lower-third graphic, even after I swear I’ve already checked it. 

I mean, everyone makes mistakes sometimes, right? I'm usually really good at my job, I promise. It's just... it's happening enough lately that I got worried. Does that make sense?

symptom_reasoning.S001: The patient reports making careless technical mistakes at work, such as mislabeling camera cards and missing timecode notes, despite checking their work.

turns.doctor_question: Did you have similar difficulties with attention or making careless mistakes when you were growing up in school?
turns.patient_response:
Oh, um... well, I was never a *bad* student, I promise! I really tried to be good. But... I guess I did have a little trouble sitting still sometimes? 

It's actually kind of embarrassing to admit, but even way back in elementary school, my teachers were always having to move my desk around. It definitely wasn't because I was trying to be difficult! I just... I had a lot of energy, I guess, and I'd end up out of my seat, or I'd get too excited and just blurt out the answers. Sometimes I'd end up bothering my classmates before I even realized I was doing it. 

I was just really eager to participate, I think. I didn't mean any harm by it. Does that... is that the kind of thing you're asking about?

symptom_reasoning.S011: The patient states they had trouble sitting still and would end up out of their seat in elementary school.
symptom_reasoning.S016: The patient admits they would get too excited and blurt out answers in class.
symptom_reasoning.S018: The patient mentions they would end up bothering their classmates before realizing they were doing it.

turns.doctor_question: Nowadays as an adult, do you still feel that sense of physical restlessness or have trouble sitting still for long periods?
turns.patient_response:
Oh, um... well, I mean, I can sit still when I really need to! I'm a professional, I promise, I don't just run around the edit bay or anything. But... I guess, if I'm being completely honest, it does get a little... tricky sometimes? 

Like, if I have to sit through a long client screening... I know I’m supposed to just sit there and watch the cut quietly, and I really do try my best to be respectful and attentive. But sometimes it feels like there’s this... this pressure building up right under my skin? It's almost like my body is just begging me to get up and do something, anything, even though I know I absolutely shouldn't. 

I usually manage to hide it, I think. I just sort of power through. I hope that doesn't make me sound immature or like a bad employee. Is that... is that a normal thing to feel at my age?

symptom_reasoning.S012: The patient describes a physical pressure under their skin and a strong internal urge to get up and move when required to sit still.
symptom_reasoning.S011: The patient explicitly states they do not run around and manage to stay seated ('power through') when expected to remain seated.

turns.doctor_question: Outside of work, do you notice similar challenges, like misplacing everyday items, being forgetful with chores, or having trouble organizing your personal life?
turns.patient_response:
Oh, um... outside of work? Honestly, I think I'm pretty okay there. I mean, I really try to keep things together at home. I wouldn't say my personal life is a mess or anything! 

I guess... I mean, maybe sometimes I'll misplace my keys or my phone for a minute, but everyone does that, right? Especially when you're busy or tired from a long day. I really do try to stay on top of my chores and keep my apartment nice. I don't think I'm any more forgetful than the average person when it comes to that stuff. 

I just... I really want to be responsible, you know? I hope I'm answering your questions right. I just wouldn't want you to think I'm completely disorganized in every part of my life.

symptom_reasoning.S005: The patient denies being disorganized in their personal life, stating they keep things together at home.
symptom_reasoning.S007: The patient denies frequently losing items, stating they only misplace keys or phones occasionally like anyone else.
symptom_reasoning.S009: The patient denies being forgetful with daily activities, stating they stay on top of chores and are not more forgetful than average.

turns.doctor_question: Do you find it difficult to keep your attention focused on tasks, especially when working on long or repetitive projects?
turns.patient_response:
Oh, um... well, no, not really. I mean, I edit video for a living, so I really have to be able to focus, you know? It's my job! I wouldn't want you to think I'm bad at what I do. 

I guess... I mean, if a project is really, really repetitive, maybe my mind wanders a tiny bit? But I think that happens to everyone, right? I always make sure to get my work done on time and make it look good. I'm very dedicated to my projects. 

I really try my best to stay focused, I promise. Does that make sense? I hope that's the kind of answer you were looking for.

symptom_reasoning.S002: The patient explicitly denies having difficulty sustaining attention, stating they are able to focus well for their job as a video editor and always get their work done.

turns.doctor_question: Do you often find yourself getting easily distracted by background noises or other things going on around you while you're trying to work?
turns.patient_response:
Oh, no, I wouldn't say easily distracted. I mean, editing bays can be kind of noisy sometimes, especially if other people are working nearby or there's a lot going on in the office. But I really try to just tune it out, you know? 

I think I'm pretty good at just putting my headphones on and getting into the zone. I mean, sure, if someone drops something really loud or calls my name, I'll look up, but... that's normal, right? You'd want to know what's happening. 

I really don't let little things pull me away from what I'm doing. I always want to make sure I'm giving my full attention to the cut. I hope that sounds okay? I just wouldn't want you to think I'm sitting there staring out the window or anything!

symptom_reasoning.S008: The patient explicitly denies being easily distracted by background noises, stating they are good at tuning it out and getting into the zone.

turns.doctor_question: Do you often find yourself interrupting other people or blurting out responses before they have finished speaking?
turns.patient_response:
Oh, um... well, maybe a little bit? But I think it's just because I'm so eager to help, you know? Like, I really want to be on the same page as everyone else. 

Sometimes, if a director or a client is asking me something, I... I guess I might jump in with an answer before they're totally finished? But it's only because I want to show them I'm engaged and ready to fix whatever they need. I just get really enthusiastic about the work! 

I mean, every now and then, I'll realize halfway through my sentence that I'm actually answering the wrong thing because I just reacted to the first few words they said... but I always correct myself right away! I really hope that doesn't make me sound rude or anything. I just want to be helpful and quick. Is it normal to get a little ahead of yourself when you're excited about a project?

symptom_reasoning.S016: The patient admits to jumping in with answers before a director or client has finished their question, often reacting to just the first few words.
